_meta.description: Structured companion to references/testing_indications.md. Routes a clinical picture to the authority that makes genetic testing indicated, and routes a test already done to what it could not have found. Deliberately contains NO eligibility wording, NO age thresholds, and NO diagnostic yield figures — those drift between directory versions and must be retrieved from the cited authority with a retrieval date.

how_to_read.url: Present when the exact location is known and stable. Fetch it.
how_to_read.find_by: Present when the document is named precisely but the URL is not recorded. Search for the named document rather than guessing a link.
how_to_read.establishes: What the authority is being cited FOR. Never cite it for more than this.
how_to_read.trigger_groups: Every group must have at least one hit for the indication to match. Two groups means two independent features must both be present — 'autism' alone must not match the with-developmental-delay indication.
how_to_read.absent_triggers: If any of these appear, the indication does NOT match. Absence of a phrase is not evidence that the feature is absent, so an indication matched this way is reported with that caveat rather than asserted.
how_to_read.reanalysable: Whether the assay left data that can be re-examined. False means reanalysis is the wrong request and new testing is the right one — a distinction that decides whether an ask succeeds.

ACMG_2021.name: Exome and genome sequencing for pediatric patients with congenital anomalies or intellectual disability: an evidence-based clinical guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (Manickam et al.)
ACMG_2021.establishes: Exome or genome sequencing recommended as a first- or second-tier test for congenital anomalies, developmental delay and intellectual disability in paediatric patients

NHS_NGTD.name: NHS National Genomic Test Directory (rare and inherited disease)
NHS_NGTD.jurisdiction: England; Scotland, Wales and NI operate related but separate arrangements
NHS_NGTD.establishes: Which test is commissioned for which clinical indication, and the eligibility criteria a patient must meet. This is the operative document for NHS access — it states eligibility explicitly, and it is revised periodically.
NHS_NGTD.find_by: Search 'NHS National Genomic Test Directory rare and inherited disease' on england.nhs.uk for the current version and its eligibility criteria document. OUTSIDE ENGLAND this document does not govern: for Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland, cite ACMG 2021 for the clinical recommendation and establish the access route with the local clinical genetics service rather than naming a framework you have not retrieved.

ACMG_SF.name: ACMG SF v3.3 list for reporting of secondary findings in clinical exome and genome sequencing
ACMG_SF.establishes: Which genes are reported as secondary findings, and that opting in or out is a consent decision taken before testing

ACMG_FRAGILE_X.name: ACMG technical standards for fragile X (FMR1) testing
ACMG_FRAGILE_X.establishes: That FMR1 repeat sizing is a distinct assay from sequencing, and when it is indicated
ACMG_FRAGILE_X.find_by: Search ACMG technical standards FMR1 fragile X testing for the current version

asd_with_dd_or_id.label: Autism spectrum diagnosis with developmental delay or intellectual disability
notes: This is the core case the skill exists for. Around 11.3% of people evaluated receive guideline-concordant testing (Arcebido et al., Autism, 2025), and the barriers found were insurance status and race rather than clinical need.
traps: A previous normal microarray does not close this out — it cannot detect sequence variants at all.
FMR1 repeat sizing is a separate assay and is frequently omitted. If the indication is autism or ID and there is no separate FMR1 result, that is a gap worth naming.

asd_without_dd_or_id.label: Autism spectrum diagnosis without developmental delay or intellectual disability
notes: Genuinely more contested than the case above, and eligibility differs between systems. Retrieve the current criteria rather than assuming; say plainly that this one depends on the system and on other features.
traps: Do not present testing as clearly indicated here when it may not be. Overstating eligibility sets a family up for a refusal they were told would not happen.

dysmorphism_or_congenital_anomaly.label: Dysmorphic features, congenital anomalies, or organ malformation
notes: One of the strongest indications, and named explicitly in ACMG 2021.

epilepsy_with_ndd.label: Epilepsy alongside developmental delay or regression
notes: Often the indication with the most immediate management consequence, because a result can change antiseizure medication choice.
traps: A panel is fixed at its version date. If the panel predates the relevant gene's description, a normal panel result means less than it appears to.

family_history.label: Family history of a neurodevelopmental condition or a known familial variant
commonly_indicated: targeted testing for the known familial variant
notes: Where a specific familial variant is known, targeted testing for that variant is a different and usually simpler request than broad sequencing.
traps: Testing an unaffected relative — particularly a child — is a genetic counselling conversation before it is a testing request. Route it rather than drafting a request.

prior_nondiagnostic_reanalysis.label: Previous non-diagnostic testing, now potentially due for reanalysis
commonly_indicated: broader testing than was originally performed
notes: Nobody proactively recalls these families; no system has that mechanism. Gene discovery has moved substantially since 2021-22, so a non-diagnostic result more than roughly two years old is worth actively asking about.
traps: Reanalysis of existing data and new testing are different requests with different costs. Establish which is being asked for.
Do not recommend reanalysis of a recent report. Check the report date first.

karyotype.label: Karyotype
cannot_detect: most copy number variants below microscopic resolution
karyotype.note: Misses almost everything relevant to a neurodevelopmental indication.
karyotype.reanalysis_note: Produces no sequence data, so there is nothing to reanalyse. The ask here is new testing, not reanalysis.

fish.label: FISH
detects: the specific region it was targeted at
fish.note: Targeted by design. A normal FISH says nothing about the rest of the genome.
fish.reanalysis_note: Produces no sequence data, so there is nothing to reanalyse. The ask here is new testing, not reanalysis.

microarray.label: Chromosomal microarray (CMA)
detects: copy number variants above the platform's resolution
microarray.note: A normal microarray is not a completed genetic workup. This is the single most common gap in an autism or ID pathway.
microarray.reanalysis_note: Produces no sequence data, so there is nothing to reanalyse. The ask here is new testing, not reanalysis.

panel.label: Targeted gene panel
detects: variants in the genes on the panel, as of the panel's version date
cannot_detect: genes described after the panel version
copy number depending on the pipeline
panel.note: Ask which panel and which version. Panels age badly, and the version date is the operative fact.
panel.reanalysis_note: Leaves sequence data that can be re-examined against current knowledge without a new sample.

exome.label: Exome sequencing (ES)
detects: some copy number variants depending on the pipeline
exome.note: Singleton exome without parental samples materially limits interpretation. Whether it was a trio matters.
exome.reanalysis_note: Leaves sequence data that can be re-examined against current knowledge without a new sample.

genome.label: Genome sequencing (GS)
cannot_detect: many repeat expansions on short reads
methylation abnormalities without a separate assay
genome.note: Broadest short-read test, still not exhaustive.
genome.reanalysis_note: Leaves sequence data that can be re-examined against current knowledge without a new sample.

fmr1_repeat.label: FMR1 repeat sizing
detects: FMR1 CGG repeat expansion and its methylation status
fmr1_repeat.note: A separate assay. Its absence from a workup is a gap in its own right, not a detail.
fmr1_repeat.reanalysis_note: Produces no sequence data, so there is nothing to reanalyse. The ask here is new testing, not reanalysis.
